topic.title: Only three units left
topic.claim: 'Only three units left at this price' at a site visit is a price ladder, not a shortage.
topic.moment: The sales lady says the price goes up next week, and the cheque book suddenly feels urgent.

turn.actually: Builders release stock in slabs and raise the price each slab, so 'last units' is always true.

topic.feeling: Rushed into the biggest cheque of my life.
topic.villain: Phased inventory releases built into builder pricing
topic.because: Each price step rewards early buyers on paper and pushes late ones to hurry. The builder controls how many units are 'left'.
topic.payoff: Ask how many units are unreleased, not how many are left.
topic.behaviour: Builders announce price hikes by phase and run 'limited' offers at site visits.
topic.send_to: The couple doing site visits every Sunday
topic.why_now: Festive launches just pushed a wave of 'new phase' pricing.

score.why: 'Last units' is always true because the builder controls what's released. The sharp question to ask is how many units are unreleased.
